# Set Up

```{r}
#load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(emmeans)

typevector <- c(1, 2, 1, 4, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 2, 2, 3, 4, 3, 4, 3)

data <- data.frame(Type = factor(x = typevector, 
                                    levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4), 
                                    labels = c("alkaline, name brand",
                                                    "alkaline, store brand", 
                                                    "heavy duty, name brand", 
                                                    "heavy duty, store brand")
                                    ),
                  Time = c(602, 863, 529, 235, 534, 585, 743, 232, 282, 773, 840, 
                           255, 238, 200, 228, 215),
                  Cost = c(0.985, 0.935, 0.985, 0.495, 0.985, 0.985, 0.935, 0.520, 
                           0.495, 0.935, 0.935, 0.520, 0.495, 0.520, 0.495, 0.520),
                  CostPerUnit = c(611, 923, 537, 476, 542, 593, 794, 445, 569, 827,
                                  898, 490, 480, 384, 460, 413),
                  Order = seq(from = 1, to = 16, by = 1)
                  )
data <- data |>
                      mutate(Duty = case_when(
                        Type %in% c("alkaline, name brand", 
                                    "alkaline, store brand") ~ "alkaline",
                        Type %in% c("heavy duty, name brand", 
                                    "heavy duty, store brand") ~ "heavy duty",
                        TRUE ~ NA_character_),
                        Brand = case_when(
                          Type %in% c("alkaline, name brand", 
                                      "heavy duty, name brand") ~ "name",
                          Type %in% c("alkaline, store brand", 
                                      "heavy duty, store brand") ~ "store",
                          TRUE ~ NA_character_)
                          )
data
```

# Q1

```{r}
# Use aggregate to calculate the average value of Life Per Unit Cost for each of 
# the four treatment combinations
means <- result <- aggregate(CostPerUnit ~ Type + Brand, 
                             data = data, 
                             FUN = mean)
means
```

# Q2

```{r}
# Use interaction.plot to create an interaction plot with Duty on the x-axis 
# and two lines, one for each Brand
interaction.plot(
  x.factor     = data$Duty,        # Variable on the X-axis
  trace.factor = data$Brand,       # Variable that creates the separate lines
  response     = data$CostPerUnit,       # Numeric dependent variable (Y-axis)
  fun          = mean,           # Summary statistic to plot (default is mean)
  type         = "b",            # "b" plots both points and lines
  col          = c("blue", "red", "limegreen"), # Colors for the two Brand lines
  pch          = c(16, 16, 16),      # Point symbols for the lines
  lty          = 1,              # Line type (solid)
  lwd          = 5,              # Line width
  xlab         = "Duty Level",   # X-axis label
  ylab         = "Mean Cost Per Unit",   # Y-axis label
  trace.label  = "Brand"         # Title for the legend box
)
```

# Q7

```{r}
# Duty Main effect
DutyMain <- (1/2) * means$CostPerUnit[1] + (1/2) * means$CostPerUnit[2] - (1/2) *means$CostPerUnit[3] - (1/2) *means$CostPerUnit[4]
DutyMain
```

# Q8

```{r}
# Use aov()  to fit the effects model with the response “Life per unit cost.” Use 
# emmeans and contrast to verify your estimates from problems 5 and 7.
# Fit the two-factor effects model with interaction
battery_model <- aov(CostPerUnit ~ Duty * Brand, data = data)

# Extract Estimated Marginal Means (Cell Means / Problem 5)
cell_means <- emmeans(battery_model, ~ Duty * Brand)
cell_means
# The estimates are nearly identicaly and very due to rounding.

# Verify the Main Effect of Duty (Problem 7 Contrast)
# This uses the specific weights [0.5, 0.5, -0.5, -0.5] we defined earlier
duty_contrast <- contrast(cell_means, method = list(
  "Main Effect of Duty" = c(0.5, 0.5, -0.5, -0.5)
))
duty_contrast

# The Contrast results in nearly the same estimate for the main effect.
```
